Title: THE ENIGMATIC SMILE
AnswerDetails: Real title: Mona Lisa (La Gioconda), Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1503-1519, Louvre, Paris. Trivia: it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 by Vincenzo Peruggia, a former museum workman, and the two years it spent missing are much of the reason it is the most famous painting in the world.

Title: A SWIRLING NIGHT SKY
AnswerDetails: Real title: The Starry Night, Vincent van Gogh, 1889, Museum of Modern Art, New York. Trivia: van Gogh painted it from the window of his room at the Saint-Paul asylum in Saint-Remy-de-Provence, where he had admitted himself voluntarily the year before.

Title: THE TOWERING SEA
AnswerDetails: Real title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa (Under the Wave off Kanagawa), from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, Katsushika Hokusai, c. 1831. Trivia: it is a woodblock print rather than a painting, so thousands of impressions were pulled - and the small peak in the trough of the wave is Mount Fuji, which most people miss on first look.

Title: A GLANCE OVER THE SHOULDER
AnswerDetails: Real title: Girl with a Pearl Earring, Johannes Vermeer, c. 1665, Mauritshuis, The Hague. Trivia: it is not a portrait but a tronie - a study of a type or a costume rather than of a named sitter - so nobody knows who she was, or whether she was anyone at all.

Title: ARRIVAL ON THE SHORE
AnswerDetails: Real title: The Birth of Venus, Sandro Botticelli, c. 1485, Uffizi, Florence. Trivia: Botticelli painted it on canvas at a time when Florentine works on this scale were normally painted on wooden panel.

Title: A CRY ON THE BRIDGE
AnswerDetails: Real title: The Scream, Edvard Munch, 1893, National Museum, Oslo. Trivia: the figure is not the one screaming. Munch's own note describes hearing a scream passing through nature and covering his ears against it. He made several versions, in paint and in pastel, plus a lithograph.

Title: AN EMBRACE IN GOLD
AnswerDetails: Real title: The Kiss (Der Kuss), Gustav Klimt, 1907-1908, Belvedere, Vienna. Trivia: the gold leaf belongs to Klimt's golden phase, which followed a trip to Ravenna and its Byzantine mosaics.

Title: ABOVE THE CLOUDS
AnswerDetails: Real title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, Caspar David Friedrich, c. 1818, Kunsthalle Hamburg. Trivia: the hidden face is the point. Friedrich's Ruckenfigur device puts the viewer in the man's place looking out, and who he was meant to be has never been settled.

Title: THE COMPANY STEPS OUT
AnswerDetails: Real title: The Night Watch (Militia Company of District II under the Command of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq), Rembrandt van Rijn, 1642, Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Trivia: it is not a night scene - darkened varnish earned it that nickname - and in 1715 it was cut down on all four sides to fit a wall in Amsterdam's town hall, losing two figures from the left edge.

Title: AN AFTERNOON IN THE PARK
AnswerDetails: Real title: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte, Georges Seurat, 1884-1886, Art Institute of Chicago. Trivia: Seurat worked on it for about two years and made dozens of preparatory studies, then later added a painted border of dots so the picture would not have to sit against a conventional frame.
